songs.title: Coyote
sections: or why I crossed the road — This is for Late Bloom. It's never too late—

I ought to be used to this by now
The "might as well give up" suffocation
The finger pointing relay
The "well you're the one who's…"
Time bomb
The tears

I can listen to the same break up playlist
And feel the same helplessness
Now with him, instead of him
And myself, mostly

I should really have a routine by now
A little rehearsed skit about lost loves
About how it takes more love to let go
Than to hold on
About how much we learned
Thank you
And goodbye

But each time is like getting hit by a Mack truck
Like the Coyote in the cartoons
First by a red truck, then by a green one
Over and over
Looking one way and then, BAM!
Fucked
By another one

Over and over again
Until it's kind of funny
Like the cartoons
Comic.

He blinks at the sun,
ears ringing, dust settling.
Brushes gravel from his cheek,
nudges his snout back into place.
Coughs, tastes the desert.
Shakes his head — never again.
Then a rustle of feathers,
a flash of blue and gold.
Something stirs — hunger? mischief?
Before the thought has a name,
he's already running.

And maybe it's always been like this —
stories that never explain themselves.
The coyote and the bird.
The vows we make at twenty, thirty, forty,
as if we could map the rest of our lives
in matching lines and parallel change.
We call it happily ever after.
But it's a coin toss at best,
a myth we keep retelling.

Over and over again
Until it's kind of funny
Like the cartoons
Comic.
